question.problem:
A curve is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=7(t-1),\,y=2{t}^{3}-18t,\,-\infty <t<\infty .
$$

Determine the points at which the normal to the curve is vertical.
question.worked_solution:
The normal is vertical if the tangent is horizontal. Therefore, we require ${y}^{′}(t)=0$ while ${x}^{′}(t)\ne 0.$

So, we first find the derivatives of $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=7,\,{y}^{′}(t)=6{t}^{2}-18.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving ${y}^{′}(t)=0$ gives

$$
6({t}^{2}-3)=0\,⟹\,t=\pm \sqrt{3}.
$$

Now, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(-\sqrt{3}) & =7\ne 0, \\ {x}^{′}(\sqrt{3}) & =7\ne 0,\end{aligned}
$$

which confirms that the normal to the curve is indeed vertical when $t=\pm \sqrt{3}.$
